registeredBy: Sam (owner); registered before any run of this version
hypothesis: An AR (lag 0-13 by BIC) forecast of monthly y/y inflation, fitted on the last 10 years at each origin, has a lower RMSE than carrying the newest figure on, 3 and 12 months ahead.

retestOf.verdict: failed (relative RMSE 3.415 at 3 months and 6.232 at 12 months against no change, p 1)
retestOf.change: Fits on the last 120 months (10 years) at each origin instead of the whole history. Version 1 fitted each country's full OECD history, which includes the 1980s-90s hyperinflations (Brazil, Argentina, Turkey, Poland and others at hundreds to thousands of percent); those episodes set the AR coefficients and error spread for today's forecasts. Ten years is the window the policy-rate model was already registered with. Everything else is as in version 1.

knownLimits: Values are today's vintage (later revisions included); no real-time data vintages are free for all countries, so this is a pseudo real-time test.
Inflation is close to a random walk in many countries over these horizons, so the naive benchmark is hard to beat.
Not compared with past IMF WEO forecasts: the app holds only today's WEO vintage, so an IMF benchmark cannot be scored without look-ahead. A later version can add it once past vintages are stored.
A re-test drafted after version 1 failed, so it carries less weight than a first test: one change, chosen on a stated principle, and no further versions will be tried if it fails.
